1.evidence_source: The current study examined the relationships between gender ideology and body image in a sample of British female undergraduates.
1._section_summary: This abstract reports a single study of British female undergraduates (n = 135) who completed the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and the Femininity Ideology Scale (FIS). Significant negative correlations were found between body appreciation and respondent BMI (rs = -0.17 to -0.26) and between BAS and several FIS scores; BMI and Stereotypic Images and Activities together explained 10.0% of variance in body appreciation. The abstract does not report survey method, mean age, participant ethnicity percentages, or mean BMI.
